links.outcome: Reading grade level of original trial consent forms versus eighth-grade target
links.effect: Mean Flesch-Kincaid level 11.52 for original ICFs; only 1 (2%) at or below eighth grade. GPT-edited mean 9.47; 18 (39%) at or below eighth grade.
links.quote: Only 1 (2%) of the original ICFs and 18 (39%) of the GPT-edited ICFs had a Flesch-Kincaid reading level at or below eighth grade (P<0.001).

links.outcome: Readability of AI-edited consent materials versus originals, with semantic similarity
links.effect: Flesch-Kincaid grade 11.52 original vs 9.47 GPT-edited (P<0.001); mean semantic similarity 0.85 (SD=0.04).
links.quote: Mean reading levels were 11.52 for the original and 9.47 for the GPT-edited ICFs using the Flesch-Kincaid grade level (P<0.001).

unlisted_practices: Using a customized GPT to simplify clinical trial informed consent form readability

screen.reason: Evaluates using a customized GPT-4o model to simplify clinical trial informed consent forms to improve readability scores, compared to original forms, without testing deployment practices or clinical human interaction.
